sections.h2: How does selling a house in Cheltenham work?
sections.html:
A Cheltenham sale follows the normal Pennsylvania steps, with one township requirement layered in: the seller must hand the buyer zoning and use certifications issued by the township before settlement. Cheltenham is a home-rule township in the southeast corner of Montgomery County, so the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds records the deed and the county Board of Assessment Appeals handles values.

Allow time for paperwork, because a seller who needs to close quickly should file the township application as soon as there is a signed agreement of sale and a settlement date. The township's code says it will issue the certification statement and affidavits within 15 days of receiving the application, and no deed is registered by the township until the certifications are issued.

Cheltenham is a 9.03-square-mile inner-ring suburb that borders Philadelphia on the south and east, Abington Township and Jenkintown on the north and Springfield Township on the west. Fifteen Quakers from Cheltenham, England, bought the land from William Penn in 1682, and Tookany Creek powered the mills that shaped early settlement.

Cheltenham became a first-class township in 1900 and a home-rule municipality in 1976. It has no mayor; a Board of Commissioners with one member from each of seven wards governs it, and a separate school board runs the schools. Sellers can reach the township office at 215-887-1000 on weekdays for permit questions.

The township has ten districts: Glenside, Laverock, Edge Hill, Wyncote, Cedarbrook, Chelten Hills, La Mott, Elkins Park, Melrose Park and Cheltenham Village. Zip codes are 19012, 19027, 19038 and 19095. Wealthy Philadelphians built estates here in the late nineteenth century, among them Lynnewood Hall, the Elkins estate and Grey Towers Castle, and the later housing stock includes rowhouses, twins and split levels. Cheltenham Township School District runs the public schools, ending at Cheltenham High School, and Arcadia University is in Glenside.

sections.h2: How good is transit from Cheltenham?
sections.html:
Transit is a selling point here, because SEPTA Regional Rail runs through the township and all lines north of Center City except Trenton pass through it. Stations carry the names of neighborhoods such as Glenside, Melrose Park and Jenkintown-Wyncote.

  • Bus: SEPTA City Division routes start at the Cheltenham-Ogontz bus loop at Ogontz Avenue (PA 309) and Cheltenham Avenue.
  • Roads: Cheltenham Avenue is the border with Philadelphia and links to PA 611 and PA 309; Old York Road, Limekiln Pike and Willow Grove Avenue continue from the city.
  • Commute: workers average 30.6 minutes each way, per the Census Bureau.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Cheltenham housing?
sections.html:
These figures are the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates for the township. About 62.6 percent of housing units are owner occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $384,800.

Median gross rent is $1,608 and median household income is $109,022. There are 14,859 households averaging 2.47 people, and 58.1 percent of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree. The population was 37,452 in 2020 and an estimated 38,498 in July 2025, up 2.9 percent from the base.

sections.h2: What must a Cheltenham seller deliver at settlement?
sections.html:
Chapter 217 of the Cheltenham Township code, titled Property, Sale of, makes it unlawful to sell without delivering four items to the buyer at or before settlement. The township issues them on forms it provides and may inspect, though it is not required to.

  • A certification of the property's zoning district from the township Zoning Officer.
  • A certification that the current use does or does not comply with township ordinances.
  • An affidavit that the street address number is displayed as Chapter 114 requires.
  • For a single-family home, an affidavit that smoke detectors meet the Fire Prevention Code.

The agreement of sale must state the zoning classification and warrant that the use complies. An owner who skips the certifications and whose use violated zoning faces a summary offense with a fine up to $600 plus costs. The fire code also requires battery-powered smoke detectors in single-family dwellings when they are sold. Fees are in the township's Chapter A300.

sections.h2: What if the Cheltenham house is a rental?
sections.html:
Cheltenham requires a rental license before an owner enters a rental agreement, and Chapter 227 requires every rental property to pass inspection against the building, property maintenance and fire codes at least once every three years. The license is a mercantile or business privilege license under the township's tax chapter.

  • Within 30 days of a transfer of ownership, the owner must give the Code Administrator written notice with the new owner's name and address.
  • The township gives at least seven days' notice before an inspection, and the owner schedules required inspections.
  • A license can be suspended or revoked for unpaid fees, uncorrected violations or refusing an inspection.
  • A summary offense under the chapter carries a fine of $50 to $1,000 per violation.

A landlord selling to a buyer who will keep tenants should pass along license and inspection records. Gather the last inspection report and any correction notices before you list, because the buyer's lender and inspector will ask about the house's condition.

sections.h2: What are the property tax rates in Cheltenham?
sections.html:
Cheltenham's total 2026 millage is 73.4832 mills, the highest on the county's 2026 municipal list. The table shows the pieces from the county's published list.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and permits apply in Cheltenham?
sections.html:
Montgomery County states the realty transfer tax is 2 percent, collected by the Recorder of Deeds, and Pennsylvania's share of that is 1 percent. The county page also lists the common level ratio factor, 3.36 for documents dated July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

Permits go through the township's OpenGov portal, and since March 26, 2025 the township accepts applications only there. Permits are needed for roofing, siding, decks, kitchen and bathroom renovations, fencing, sheds and HVAC. Painting, flooring and gutter replacement do not need one, and replacement windows with no change in rough opening are exempt unless the house is in a Historic District, where added review and inspection apply. A retaining wall that disturbs the Steep Slope Conservation District, a gradient of 15 percent or more, may need zoning relief first. Each permit carries a $4.50 state UCC charge. The township code also has chapters on rental licensing and inspection, sump pump standards and a vacant building registry, so landlords and owners of empty houses should check them.

faqs.q: Do I need a township certification to sell in Cheltenham?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 217 requires a zoning district certification and a use compliance certification, plus an address affidavit and, for single-family homes, a smoke detector affidavit. Apply on the township's form, and expect the answer within 15 days.

faqs.q: What happens if I skip the Cheltenham certifications?
faqs.a: The township will not register the deed, and an owner whose use violated zoning faces a summary offense with a fine up to $600 plus costs. The agreement of sale also must include the zoning and use warranty.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Cheltenham?
faqs.a: Montgomery County states the realty transfer tax is 2 percent. The Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording, with the state's 1 percent included.
Cheltenham Township School District serves the township, and its 2026-2027 millage is 56.68 mills, the largest piece of the bill.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for Cheltenham building permits?
faqs.a: On the township's OpenGov portal. Paper applications ended when the portal became mandatory on March 26, 2025, and each permit carries a $4.50 UCC charge.
